original_statement:
general i.i.d. edge-weight distributions on Z^d - the point of the paper is removing the special-distribution restriction under which such statements were previously proved
the conclusion is anti-concentration (an interval-avoidance statement), NOT a variance lower bound
the log||x|| variance lower bound it cites is available only in two dimensions

WHY THE DISTINCTION IS NOT PEDANTRY: an anti-concentration statement bounds how much mass the law of T(0,x) can put in a short interval. It does not by itself lower-bound the variance, and a variance lower bound does not by itself give anti-concentration. Chaining them silently is a category error.
METHOD: inducing a fluctuation in the number of edges in a box whose weights are of 'hi-mode' (large).
THE LITERATURE STATEMENT IS THE SECOND REASON THIS NODE EXISTS: it is a dated, first-hand confirmation from four people working directly on the problem that Newman-Piza's logarithmic bound had not been improved.
SOURCE: arXiv:1810.08270v2, 'Lower bounds for fluctuations in first-passage percolation for general distributions'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.

replacement_fragment:
Planar undirected first-passage percolation on Z^2 with independent, identically distributed nonnegative edge weights of law F. Write I=inf supp F. Assume F(0)<p_c=1/2 and, when I>0, F(I)<the oriented-bond critical threshold. Theorem 1 gives deterministic A_x,B_x such that, as ||x|| tends to infinity, liminf P(T(0,x)<=A_x)>0, liminf P(T(0,x)>=B_x)>0, and liminf (B_x-A_x)/sqrt(log ||x||)>0. If T(0,x) is square-integrable for the relevant x, these separated quantiles imply Var(T(0,x))>=c log ||x|| for all sufficiently large ||x||. Indeed, fixed positive probability lower bounds p,q and a separation L give Var(T)>=[pq/(p+q)] L^2. More generally, for a square-integrable real X, if every closed interval of length L>0 has probability at most 1-epsilon with one epsilon in (0,1], then Var(X)>=epsilon L^2/4. A variance lower bound alone need not imply anti-concentration. This statement records the planar full-lattice theorem; it makes no logarithmic lower-bound claim for higher-dimensional full lattices.
SOURCE: Damron--Hanson--Houdre--Xu, Lower bounds for fluctuations in first-passage percolation for general distributions, arXiv:1810.08270v2, condition (1.2.1) and Theorem 1.
